transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-12-15
Start time: 14:30 PST
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jenna (Redwood AE), Marcus (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood SE), Kofi (Redwood CSM) -- Aisha, Tom, Marta, Ben, Raj (Northshore)

Summary (auto): Discovery focused on reliability, fallbacks, multi-region routing, and SLA expectations. Customer evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for a latency-sensitive personalization service. Action items and benchmarking agreed.

[00:00] Jenna Ortiz: All right everyone thanks for joining. quick intro from our side, im Jenna, AE at Redwood. with me is Marcus, our solutions eng, and Priya. you all good to start?
[00:12] Aisha Khan: Yep, thanks. Aisha from Northshore. we have Tom our SRE, Marta our CTO, Ben security, and Raj product on.
[00:20] Jenna Ortiz: Awesome. high level, want to understand your reliability needs, current pain points, and timelines.
[00:27] Marta Silva: Sure. We're building a personalization layer that serves model-inferred recommendations inline with checkout. P95 latency needs to be under 120ms, P99 under 300ms. major concern is maintaining availability during infra incidents. we need failovers and clear SLA promises.
[00:45] Marcus Li: Got it. are you currently serving from a cloud endpoint or self-hosted?
[00:50] Tom Reyes: We run a mixed setup. core inference is on our GKE self-hosted infra for tight latency control, but we've been exploring managed endpoints because ops overhead is high.
[01:00] Raj Patel: also cost is a consideration. If we move to managed, want to avoid 3x token cost for small quality gains.
[01:08] Priya Anand: totally fair. for reliability we typically talk about three levers: routing policies (multi-region), model fallbacks (lighter quantized variants), and capacity tiers (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private).
[01:20] Ben Cho: Quick Q on encryption and audit. We need KMS integration and end-to-end audit logs for every request. SOC 2 compliance.
[01:28] Jenna Ortiz: Redwood supports KMS/HSM integrations for Private and Dedicated; Hosted supports customer-managed keys via BYOK in certain tiers. We also have audit logs and trace ids for every request. we'll share the SOC2 report afterwards.
[01:40] Marta Silva: Great. can you explain how fallbacks work? for example during a region outage do you re-route to another region? how do you preserve session state / KV cache?
[01:50] Marcus Li: Good question. Our smart routing layer allows policy-driven failover. simplest pattern: route by latency first, then region fallback if a region is unhealthy. for session continuity we persist KV cache in a regional store and replicate lightweight checkpoints to an adjacent region; there's a small cold-start penalty when you failover and you may lose recent incremental KV until it's warmed.
[02:15] Tom Reyes: How small is small? we're sensitive to a 100ms regressed P99.
[02:20] Marcus Li: Typical warm-up is 200-400ms depending on model and sequence lengths. with pre-warmed standby pools we can keep that under 150ms for common sessions. there's an engineering tradeoff — prewarming costs money.
[02:35] Raj Patel: So that implies cost vs latency tradeoff, makes sense. What about model fallback if the heavy model is saturated?
[02:43] Priya Anand: We maintain model variant chains, e.g., redwood-large -> redwood-medium-quant -> redwood-small-quant. Our runtime supports automatic semantic-preserving fallbacks and you can configure quality thresholds to stop fallback if unacceptable. Also we do dustbin scoring to detect hallucination increase.
[03:03] Aisha Khan: Are those open-source models or proprietary?
[03:07] Marcus Li: Mostly open models we curate and verify performance on. we label variants and their expected latency/cost profiles. sometimes customers bring their own fine-tuned models to any deployment mode.
[03:15] Ben Cho: For Private deployment in our VPC, do you still manage the control plane? what visibility do we get?
[03:21] Jenna Ortiz: In Private we offer a customer-managed control plane option. you can run the control plane in your VPC and we can run the orchestration components either as images you deploy or through a managed option. logging, metrics, and audit are pushed to your observability endpoint.
[03:34] Ben Cho: And SLA? for Dedicated we need a 99.95% uptime SLA across our critical endpoints.
[03:40] Kofi Mensah: We do offer SLA-backed Dedicated capacity packages. 99.95% is within the scope of our enterprise contracts, with credits and runbooks. SLA specifics depend on region and capacity commitment; we'll share standard wording.
[03:52] Marta Silva: Suppose there's a whole-region outage in us-west1. Will traffic move to eu-west or us-east and how do you handle data residency concerns?
[04:02] Marcus Li: Routing is policy-driven — you can restrict failover to only certain regions to honor data residency. if the policy allows it we'll route to us-east first, then other allowed regions. Also we can configure masking strategies where sensitive requests only run in specific zones and fail closed if not available.
[04:20] Tom Reyes: You mentioned pre-warmed standby. is that per-tenant or shared?
[04:25] Priya Anand: We support both. for Dedicated we can reserve per-tenant standby pools. for Hosted it's multi-tenant pre-warmed nodes with isolation guarantees. if you require strict isolation it's usually Dedicated or Private.
[04:38] Raj Patel: How do you instrument latency SLOs and alerting so our SREs can own runbooks?
[04:44] Marcus Li: We export per-request traces, token-level timings, and breakdowns by model and route. you can feed to your Prometheus/Grafana or use our console. We'll provide pre-built dashboards and runbook templates for typical flapping scenarios and for failover testing.
[05:05] Aisha Khan: Do you have examples of real incidents and how Redwood handled failover?
[05:10] Jenna Ortiz: Yes, we have an incident postmortem repository and a few anonymized case studies - I'll attach the reliability playbook and one recent postmortem where our multi-region routing avoided a >2hr outage.
[05:20] Marta Silva: Please do. also curious about testing — can we simulate region failovers and traffic shapers?
[05:26] Marcus Li: Absolutely. we run synthetic chaos tests and can run a simulated failover in staging with your test set. that will show cold-start impact and fallback success rates.
[05:36] Tom Reyes: Metrics we'd like to see: failover time, percent requests hitting fallback model, error spike maps.
[05:43] Priya Anand: We'll include those in the benchmark report.
[05:47] Raj Patel: On the security side, can you do SSO/SAML and RBAC to tie to our IdP?
[05:52] Jenna Ortiz: Yes, SSO + SAML + SCIM provisioning and RBAC are supported across Dedicated and Private; Hosted supports SSO and role controls too.
[06:00] Ben Cho: What's the data retention policy for logs in Hosted vs Private?
[06:05] Kofi Mensah: Hosted has configurable retention tiers; enterprise customers can request longer retention. Private you control retention via your observability stack.
[06:12] Marta Silva: Cost question again — for pre-warmed standby and multi-region replication, ballpark how much higher is cost vs base?
[06:18] Marcus Li: Pre-warmed standby typically adds ~20-60% overhead depending on standby size; multi-region replication overhead is a factor of the number of replicas plus egress. We can model scenarios once you provide traffic curves.
[06:32] Aisha Khan: Timeline — we want a pilot by end of Q1 with 1 region, then add cross-region failover in Q2. is that feasible?
[06:40] Jenna Ortiz: Yes that matches typical customers. pilot on Hosted/Dedicated to evaluate then decide on Dedicated/Private for production.
[06:46] Marta Silva: For pilot, will you allow access to raw latency logs and token-level traces? we need that for SRE analysis.
[06:52] Marcus Li: Yes, during pilot you'll get full trace access, and we can run a benchmark with your prompt set.
[06:58] Tom Reyes: For the failover scenario, curious how session continuity behaves for chat-like stateful workloads — you mentioned KV replication but that could lag. any mitigation for critical state?
[07:09] Priya Anand: For critical state we recommend a dual-write to your authoritative store with TTLs and to the KV cache. That way if failover occurs the authoritative store allows reconstruction. There's small added latency on write but it's an option for strict consistency.
[07:23] Raj Patel: We're worried about SLA credits not being meaningful if the outage is partial. how do you define endpoint availability in your SLA?
[07:30] Kofi Mensah: SLA is measured per endpoint/route and takes into account latency targets and error rates. We'll share the SLA doc; typically credit triggers when availability drops below threshold for a defined window.
[07:42] Marta Silva: Do you support canary rollouts and automatic fallback to previous model if quality drops?
[07:47] Marcus Li: Yes. rollouts with canary percentages, automatic metrics-based rollback, and routing policies that can split traffic by user cohort or route.
[07:55] Ben Cho: Are audit logs tamper-evident?
[07:58] Jenna Ortiz: We timestamp and sign logs; for Private we can integrate with your HSM for signing.
[08:05] Aisha Khan: There's been mention of vendor lock-in; how easy is it for us to export models and traces if we leave?
[08:13] Priya Anand: We provide export tools for traces, model artifacts and request logs. For model weights, it depends on licensing of the model. For your own models you can always bring them back.
[08:25] Raj Patel: any limitations on model size in Hosted?
[08:29] Marcus Li: Hosted has supported model size ranges; very large models (>70B) are usually Dedicated or Private due to GPU memory profiles.
[08:36] Tom Reyes: Can we run a pressure test that saturates the model to force fallback and measure end-user impact?
[08:40] Marcus Li: Yes we'd do that as part of the benchmark sim — we'll orchestrate traffic patterns to push to saturation and validate fallback chain behavior.
[08:48] Marta Silva: Who owns the canary rollback automation? is that on our side or Redwood's?
[08:53] Jenna Ortiz: Redwood ships the automation; you can choose to run it managed or control it yourself in Private.
[08:59] Aisha Khan: Okay, I think we've got the gist. Can you send a summary of recommended config for our workload?
[09:04] Jenna Ortiz: We'll send a recommended configuration: pilot on Hosted with pre-warmed standby, then Dedicated for production with per-tenant standby and cross-region replication. I'll include cost estimates.
[09:15] Marta Silva: Please also include a recommended SLO and runbook template.
[09:18] Kofi Mensah: we'll attach runbook templates and a sample postmortem.
[09:23] Ben Cho: Scheduling security deep-dive next week would be ideal.
[09:26] Jenna Ortiz: We'll propose slots.
[09:28] -- brief silence while people nod --
[09:32] Transcript imperfections / crosstalk: (Tom) "so like when we failover it doesn't..." (Marcus) "it does, but there's a small warm up" (unlabelled) laughter
[09:40] Jenna Ortiz: Recap - action items: Marcus to run cross-region fallback sim and provide logs; Jenna to send pricing + SLA doc + reliability playbook; Aisha to share traffic profile and success criteria; schedule security deep dive.
[09:55] Aisha Khan: Sounds good. one last thing — for Dedicated contract are there minimum commitments?
[10:00] Jenna Ortiz: Yes typically monthly or annual commits. we'll include both options.
[10:05] Marta Silva: thanks everyone, we'll review the docs.
[10:08] Jenna Ortiz: thanks all.

References shared: reliability_playbook.pdf (link), SLA_dedicated_v2.docx (link), benchmark_template.xlsx (link), anonymized_postmortem.pdf (link)

End of meeting.
